claims.text: Alloying refractory HEAs with titanium improves their low-activation properties.
Alloying refractory HEAs with zirconium improves their low-activation properties.
Titanium- and zirconium-alloyed refractory HEAs are suitable for high-temperature plasma-facing components in fusion reactors.
Titanium and zirconium additions alter the microstructural stability of refractory HEAs.
Titanium and zirconium additions alter the phase composition of refractory HEAs.
Adding titanium and zirconium enhances the thermal stability of refractory HEAs.
Adding titanium and zirconium reduces the activation levels of refractory HEAs.
Enhanced thermal stability and reduced activation improve refractory-HEA performance in fusion-reactor environments.
Titanium- and zirconium-alloyed refractory HEAs will have lower activation levels than otherwise comparable refractory HEAs without those additions.
Titanium- and zirconium-alloyed refractory HEAs will have improved high-temperature mechanical properties relative to otherwise comparable refractory HEAs without those additions.
The magnitude of the proposed improvements depends on the specific alloy composition.
The magnitude of the proposed improvements depends on processing methods.
